faq.q: Why do I get upset so easily when I am tired?
faq.a: A tired brain has an extra-jumpy alarm and weaker brakes from the thinking part. So small problems feel bigger and feelings come out faster.
asks: Why am I grumpy when I am tired?

faq.q: What does sleep do for my feelings?
faq.a: While you sleep, your brain sorts through the day's memories and feelings and resets its alarm. That is why things often feel easier in the morning.

faq.q: How much sleep do I need?
faq.a: Sleep experts suggest about 9 to 12 hours a night for children aged 6 to 12, and about 8 to 10 hours for teenagers.
asks: How many hours should a child sleep?

faq.a: Go to bed at about the same time each night, switch off screens an hour before, keep your room dark and cool, and do something calm before bed.

faq.q: What if I cannot sleep because of worries?
faq.a: Try writing your worries down or telling a grown-up before bed, then do some slow belly breathing. If you often cannot sleep, a grown-up may take you to see a doctor.
asks: Worries keep me awake at night

facts: In a 2007 study, people who missed a night of sleep had an amygdala, the brain's alarm, that reacted about 60 percent more strongly to upsetting pictures.
Sleep experts recommend 9 to 12 hours a night for children aged 6 to 12, and 8 to 10 hours for teenagers.
